messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Things are shifting quietly but clearly—can’t ignore the signs anymore. Just be careful with what you say, and keep your eyes open."
Sender 2: "The kids’ school’s back to normal, and the bus route just got extended—seems like everything’s running smoother than ever, but something feels off. I’ve been hearing whispers that even the guards are watching each other now. Keep your eyes open, but say nothing."
Sender 3: "The air’s changed — you can feel it. Things are unraveling faster than anyone thought, and people are starting to act like they finally believe it. Just keep your head down, and don’t talk about it unless you’re sure you’re alone."
Sender 4: "The markets are talking louder than usual — even the women at the stalls are naming names. Something’s shifting, and it’s not just the heat. I’ve seen the neighbor packing his bag. We should keep our heads down, but stay close."
Sender 5: "The quiet ones are getting ready — not panicking, just moving things along, like they’re expecting something to shift. The air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath but not from fear."
Sender 6: "The air’s changed — people are talking more, but quieter, like they’re testing the silence. Whatever’s coming, it’s not just rumors. Be careful what you say, and who you say it to."
Sender 7: "Just noticed how quiet the streets have gotten lately—like everyone’s holding their breath. I’ve been thinking, maybe it’s not just me; the way people are talking now, even strangers… seems like something’s shifting, but no one wants to name it."
Sender 8: "The air feels different—people aren’t just talking, they’re planning. I’ve started hearing the same quiet questions in different corners: what happens when the lights go out for good?"
Sender 9: "Just wanted to say — things feel different lately. Not loud, not dramatic, but the usual tension’s gone quiet. Even the usual noise feels… off. Maybe it’s nothing. But I’ve started noticing the small things — the way people talk, the way orders get passed around. Like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s quite ready to name it. Be careful how you speak."
Sender 10: "Just got back from the market — the usual chatter about bread prices, but this time they named the ministers. Odd, how people are starting to speak like they’re already free. The pharmacist says the shelves are clearing out, but not in a panic — more like he’s making sure he’s ready, just in case. I think we’re closer than we’ve been in years. Be careful what you say, even here."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
